messages:
support-jordan: FYI we're getting a spike of 503/500s for hosted inference (customer: acme-media). Example request-id 8f3a2bcd — user reports timeouts then 503s. Happened around 10:12 UTC. :warning:

support-jordan: error snippet from gateway: HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable - upstream reset by peer. body: "Upstream inference worker crashed (exit code 137)"

support-jordan: I collected the gateway traces and a couple request-ids, sending them here. Repro steps in case it's helpful: long context + streaming enabled.

sofia: pinging eng-oncall. @dmitri can you take a look? this smells like GPU OOM or segfaults we've seen on large-context requests.

dmitri: oncall taking. can you paste the pod list and the worker logs for one of the failed request-ids? also which model + config?

support-jordan: model: open-lingo-70b (redwood-curated), config: streaming=true, max_tokens=2048, client prompt ~= 80k chars (the customer batches multiple docs into a single request). pod list (shortened):
```
NAME                                               READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
inference-worker-0                                 1/1     Running            0          3d
inference-worker-1                                 0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   12         8h
inference-worker-2                                 1/1     Running            0          2d
```

sofia: good detail. crashloop one is the suspect.

infra-alex: grabbing recent kube events and docker logs for inference-worker-1. quick paste: 
```
-- logs --
2026-03-14T10:11:59Z [worker] INFO starting inference loop
2026-03-14T10:12:03Z [model] Allocating CUDA tensors for sequence_length=49152
2026-03-14T10:12:03Z [model] RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 32.10 GiB already allocated)
2026-03-14T10:12:03Z [worker] ERROR Unhandled exception, exiting: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/serve/runner.py", line 412, in handle_request
    outputs = model.generate(**request)
  File "/app/models/open_lingo.py", line 85, in generate
    tensor = cuda_alloc(...)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory
2026-03-14T10:12:04Z kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 1 (python) total-vm: 123456kB, anon-rss: 32000000kB, file-rss: 0kB
2026-03-14T10:12:05Z kubelet: Container killed, restartCount=12
```

infra-alex: also saw a single segfault reported earlier for a different worker: "Segmentation fault (core dumped)" in /usr/local/lib/libtorch.so. That one correlated with a host driver mismatch; current drivers look fine though.

dmitri: thanks. so we have two classes: pure GPU OOM on large-context requests, and occasional segfaults. For the immediate 503 spike it's the OOM.

maria: customer is hitting very large concatenated prompts + streaming, which means KV cache + activations blow memory. We need to both mitigate and put a guard to prevent host-level crashes.

sofia: immediate mitigation options?

dmitri: short-term: 1) add a request-level size guard on gateway to reject > 128k chars (or equivalent token limit) with 4xx and helpful message; 2) configure the worker to fallback to a smaller model variant when request_size > threshold; 3) temporarily cordon/evict the crashlooping node and drain to avoid noisy restarts.

infra-alex: I restarted the specific pod and bumped node tolerations so it won't get scheduled while we patch. Also scaled up the dedicated pool by 2 GPUs to absorb traffic.

support-jordan: customer wants a root-cause and ETA. Is there a quick patch?

dmitri: patching gateway to enforce token limit is low-risk and short. I'll open a hotfix PR to add a hard max_tokens cap and a soft warning header for customers. If we deploy that within the hour it should stop new crashes.

sofia: assign to eng-oncall for the hotfix and postmortem. also need longer-term: model-level OOM detection and graceful partial-generation fallback + server-side streaming cancellation instead of letting process get OOM-killed.

maria: for repro we tried a local script that concatenates 50 documents (~120k tokens) and used the same model; it reproduces consistently on our 40GB A100. Repro steps: `python tools/repro.py --model open-lingo-70b --prompt-file huge_prompt.txt --streaming true` -> worker crashes within 3-5s.

dmitri: can you attach the condensed repro and hardware info to the ticket? I'll include the exact stack trace and the attempted alloc sizes. Also we should mark this as Sev3->Sev2 given customer impact.

eng-oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0314-18. Priority P2. Assigned: dmitri. Updates channel: #incidents.

maria: long-term remediation ideas: quantized model variants with reduced KV memory, dynamic offloading to CPU/NVMe for very long contexts, per-request streaming throttles, and more conservative default max_input_tokens for hosted. Also need clearer customer docs about recommended batching patterns.

sofia: noting action items: dmitri hotfix gateway cap, infra-alex cordon node + scale-up, support-jordan notify customer with workaround (split documents / reduce context), maria prepare repro and perf notes, postmortem after N hours.

support-jordan: I'll message the account with a suggested workaround + ETA for the hotfix (~1hr). They appreciate the quick patch. :thumbsup:

infra-alex: follow-up: after hotfix deploy we should monitor worker restart counts and 5xx rate. I've added a temporary dashboard panel for CrashLoopBackOffs and OOM traces.

sofia: thanks team. re-open here if we see segfaults persist — may need a driver/kernel rollback plus a build with patched libtorch.

support-jordan: closing loop for now, will update when customer confirms.
